primary_number: Rp 50–300M per acute episode at Class A private hospitals (stroke/hemorrhagic: Rp 100–300M; ischemic stroke no surgery: Rp 50–150M; MI with PCI/stent: Rp 70–150M; hypertensive crisis: Rp 30–80M)
publisher: Multiple consumer-facing sources corroborated by academic INA-CBGs cost literature and private hospital group annual reports
methodology_note: No single peer-reviewed source gives per-episode private Class A hospital costs for Jakarta. Evidence assembled from: (1) Indonesian consumer health finance sources citing Rp 150–450M for severe stroke at private hospitals (CT/MRI/thrombolytics included); (2) ilovelife.co.id citing Kemenkes + WHO data: bypass surgery Rp 150–300M, stent Rp 45–75M; (3) Academic INA-CBGs studies show public hospital JKN rates of Rp 7–11M per stroke admission — private self-pay at Class A is 5–15x higher based on cost-recovery data from UI 2015 study (228% fee-for-service cost recovery vs 71% BPJS); (4) Mitra Keluarga FY2023 Annual Report: Rp 4,264.3 billion revenue / 297k inpatient admissions = ~Rp 14.4M all-in average per admission across all cases (2.8-day avg LOS), consistent with mixed-complexity billing but far below complex NCD episodes. Class A Siloam/RS Premier episodes are materially higher than MIKA average. Claim's Rp 50–200M range is broadly directionally correct but upper bound is conservative: hemorrhagic stroke with neurosurgery at Siloam/RS Premier Jatinegara can reach Rp 200–400M.
